content:
Hi everyone,

I am an undergrad at Brown working with @Rob Lewis and (hoping to become) a new contributor to Mathlib. I have opened a PR, #40911, which (in a new file) defines a predicate Algebra.HasGoingUp and proves some basic properties. My file is parallel to Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/GoingDown.lean(the theorems and proofs are almost completely analogous).

I needed this addition in a personal project as a path to proving that an injective integral homomorphism of commutative rings preserves Krull dimension; if that is of interest to Mathlib, I can PR that as well.

I'd appreciate any feedback on the PR. In particular, I had two questions:

  1. I wasn't sure where to put this work, and eventually decided to put it in a new file. I think a more natural place would be at the end of the existing Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/GoingUp.lean, but this creates an import cycle: my theorem Algebra.HasGoingUp.iff_specializingMap_primeSpectrumComap uses Mathlib.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.Topology, which itself imports Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.GoingUp.lean. What would the best solution be here?
  2. Since this work is essentially dual to Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/GoingDown.lean, I wonder if there is some unifying abstraction for the two that I am unaware of. The Stacks project does keep them separate, which motivated the decision to do so in the PR.

Welcome! Files are cheap, so it seems to a me a good idea to have a new one.

Concerning question 2 I think it would be very nice to unify them, but I don't know if it is possible (mathematically). Do you have any idea?

Riccardo Brasca said:

Concerning question 2 I think it would be very nice to unify them, but I don't know if it is possible (mathematically). Do you have any idea?

Robert and I thought about this for a bit and didn't have any clever idea, but a domain expert would know better! I don't see an obvious syntactic unification, I think if one exists it would have some mathematical content to it.
I will think about it (I know some commutative algebra but I am not an expert). Anyway I agree this is a mathematical question.

Thanks a lot for taking the time to review this!!

I haven't found any unification in the literature, but I'll keep searching (and thinking).

I would be very surprised if this exists in the literature, and I don't think we can gain any real mathematical insight (but I am very happy to be proven wrong!). On the other hand I still think it's an interesting fun question, and the formalization may become smoother. Something like the HasRankNullity class, it helps the formalization but it's quite irrelevant mathematically.

Here is my limited understanding at the moment: A map of algebras f:R→Sf : R \to Sf:R→S has the going up property if and only if the induced map f−1:Spec⁡(S)→Spec⁡(R)f^{-1} : \operatorname{Spec}(S) \to \operatorname{Spec}(R)f−1:Spec(S)→Spec(R) on prime spectra is a specializing map (this is proven in the PR); likewise, it has the going down property if and only if the induced map on prime spectra is a generalizing map. It seems that for (spectral) topological spaces, there is a notion of the Hochster dual topology, which reverses specialization order. So, given a specializing map between spectral spaces, the same underlying function becomes a generalizing map between the Hochster duals of those spaces. In our particular case, all this just amounts to reversing the order on the prime spectra of RRR and SSS.
Not sure what the above should mean for the current PR.
I had not times to look at the above today, but I plan to do so either tomorrow or on Fri
(and I meant that your description was mathematically beautiful...)
Sorry, by "the above" I meant my comment, not your comment! Apologies for being unclear.
